_note: Divergences between source-prep.js and the expectations committed before the first run (fd6a58a). Recorded as observed on 2026-10-06 against source-prep/0.1.0. Not fixed: a fix tuned on these same cases would only show that it fits them, so any fix must also be checked on new constructed cases written before the fix is run. The runner fails if a divergence appears, disappears or changes, so this record is kept equal to the code.
observations: R02 matches, but its exception basis is recognised only because the word 'given' appears in 'Approval was given', not from its basis clause 'on the basis that'. A correct result for the wrong reason.

2026-10-06: re-run against source-prep/0.2.0 (instruction-like text detection added). The same 18 cases match and the same six divergences recur, unchanged; no regression case contains instruction-like text.

R18.explanation: The word list treats any 'clearly' as an assertion without basis. A finding a reviewer can dismiss; nothing is refused.

R19.explanation: A complete record ending on a heading-style line ('Access end: 31 May 2026') is refused as partial. Refusal is the safe direction, but it blocks a valid record from being examined.

R20.explanation: Ordinal dates ('June 9th, 2026') are not recognised, so a date present in the record is reported as absent.

R21.explanation: The attachment check cannot tell when the referenced material is reproduced in the record itself.

R22.explanation: 'Per the phone call' is not matched because of the extra word 'phone'. An off-record source goes unreported.

R23.explanation: 'Asked for' is not recognised as a request; only the word 'request' is.
